roadmaps.title: The FreeBSD Handbook — one roadmap, 35 chapters
roadmaps.summary: The whole FreeBSD Handbook as one ordered path: four stages from first boot to DTrace, with a one-line promise for every chapter so you always know where you are and what it buys you.

steps.title: Introduction to FreeBSD
steps.summary: Why one permissive licence and thirty years of Unix lineage put FreeBSD inside consoles, firewalls and CDNs — and how a project with no owner ships an entire operating system.

steps.title: Installing FreeBSD
steps.summary: From image to first boot: write the media, answer bsdinstall's questions with intent — disk, network, users, hardening — and know which toggle does what before it writes to disk.

steps.title: FreeBSD Basics
steps.summary: The working vocabulary every UNIX-like system assumes: virtual consoles, accounts and groups, rwx and file flags, the directory tree, mounting, signals, and the shell that ties it all together.

steps.title: Installing Applications: Packages and Ports
steps.summary: Two roads to every application: a signed binary from pkg in seconds, or a build from Ports with exactly the options you chose. When each wins, and what to do when an install fails.

steps.title: The X Window System
steps.summary: A working graphical FreeBSD: install Xorg, pick the right driver for your GPU, skip the xorg.conf myth, and get from startx to a desktop environment or XDM login.

steps.title: Wayland on FreeBSD
steps.summary: The modern graphical FreeBSD: pick a compositor that matches how you work — Wayfire, Hikari or Sway — wire in seatd and Xwayland, and get a login screen and VNC access on top.

steps.title: Network
steps.summary: Basic wired and wireless networking on FreeBSD: hostnames, DNS, DHCP, IPv6 and how to troubleshoot a connection.

steps.title: Desktop Environments
steps.summary: Installing and configuring KDE Plasma, GNOME, Xfce, MATE, Cinnamon and LXQt, plus the usual desktop applications.

steps.title: Multimedia
steps.summary: Sound and video on FreeBSD: sound cards, mixers, audio and video players, conferencing and image scanners.

steps.title: Configuring the FreeBSD Kernel
steps.summary: When and how to build a custom kernel, what the kernel configuration file controls, and tuning the running kernel.

steps.title: Printing
steps.summary: Setting up and managing printers on FreeBSD, including the print spool, the printcap database and filters.

steps.title: Linux Binary Compatibility
steps.summary: Running Linux binaries on FreeBSD with the Linux compatibility layer, and the caveats that come with it.

steps.title: WINE
steps.summary: Running Windows applications on FreeBSD with WINE, installing it and driving it with winecfg and the file manager.

steps.title: Configuration, Services, Logging and Power Management
steps.summary: System configuration files, enabling and managing services, cron and periodic, system logging and power management.

steps.title: The FreeBSD Booting Process
steps.summary: How FreeBSD boots: the loader, kernel and init, the boot menu options and controlling the process.

steps.title: Security
steps.summary: Securing a FreeBSD system: accounts and password hashes, sudo and doas, OpenSSH and OpenSSL, IDS and Capsicum.

steps.title: Jails and Containers
steps.summary: The jail framework in depth: thick, thin, VNET and Linux jails, networking, configuration files and jail managers.

steps.title: Mandatory Access Control
steps.summary: Mandatory Access Control on FreeBSD: the framework, the available policies and how labels protect sensitive data.

steps.title: Security Event Auditing
steps.summary: Auditing security-relevant events on FreeBSD, installing and configuring the audit trail and reviewing the results.

steps.title: Storage
steps.summary: Managing storage on FreeBSD: disks, RAID, optical and tape media, memory-backed disks, network filesystems and backups.

steps.title: GEOM: Modular Disk Transformation Framework
steps.summary: The GEOM framework: providers, consumers, labels and the software RAID levels FreeBSD can build from it.

steps.title: The Z File System (ZFS)
steps.summary: ZFS explained the way it actually works: pools before datasets, redundancy fixed at pool creation, snapshots that cost nothing, and a file system that checksums every block it ever writes.

steps.title: Other File Systems
steps.summary: Non-native file systems on FreeBSD: ext2/ext3/ext4, FAT, NTFS, CD9660, FUSE and how to mount them.

steps.title: Virtualization
steps.summary: Running virtual machines on FreeBSD with bhyve, QEMU and Xen, and the bhyve management tools.

steps.title: Localization: i18n and L10n Usage and Setup
steps.summary: Using FreeBSD in languages other than English: locale classes, UTF-8, fonts, input methods and translated messages.

steps.title: Updating and Upgrading FreeBSD
steps.summary: The difference between FreeBSD-STABLE and FreeBSD-CURRENT, using freebsd-update and the source and binary upgrade paths.

steps.title: DTrace
steps.summary: Dynamic tracing on FreeBSD with DTrace: enabling it, writing scripts and using it to find performance problems.

steps.title: USB Device Mode and USB OTG
steps.summary: Turning a FreeBSD system into a USB device: device mode, USB On-The-Go and the config knobs that drive them.

steps.title: Serial Communications
steps.summary: Serial ports and terminals on FreeBSD: the uart driver, configuration files, modems and troubleshooting.

steps.title: PPP
steps.summary: Connecting FreeBSD to remote systems over PPP, with dial-up and point-to-point link configuration.

steps.title: Electronic Mail
steps.summary: Running a mail server on FreeBSD: Postfix and Sendmail, the components of an MTA and how the pieces fit together.

steps.title: Network Servers
steps.summary: Setting up FreeBSD as a network server: Apache, ftpd, Samba, NFS, DNS, NIS and time servers.

steps.title: Firewalls
steps.summary: Firewalls on FreeBSD: the philosophy, pf, IPFW and IPFilter, rulesets, NAT, tables and logging.

steps.title: Advanced Networking
steps.summary: Advanced networking topics: routing, wireless, Bluetooth, ATM, IPv6, VLANs, carrier-grade NAT and tunnelling.

steps.title: Appendices and Back Matter
steps.summary: Where to get FreeBSD, the bibliography, community resources, the OpenPGP keys of the officers and the glossary.

roadmaps.title: Linux Path — LPIC-1 Study Guide
roadmaps.summary: How to work through the ten Linux pieces in order, what each one covers and where it came from.

steps.title: Linux Origins and the Open Source Application Landscape
steps.summary: How Linux came to be, the distributions that shaped it, and the open source applications that run the world's desktops and servers.

steps.title: Open Source Licensing, ICT Skills and Working in Linux
steps.summary: Free versus open source, the licences that govern reuse, and the practical ICT skills an open source professional needs on the job.

steps.title: Command Line Basics and Getting Help
steps.summary: The anatomy of a shell command, variables, quoting, and the several ways to find help for any command you meet.

steps.title: Directories, Listing Files and Creating, Moving and Deleting Files
steps.summary: Navigate the filesystem with ls and cd, then create, rename, move, copy and delete files and directories with confidence.

steps.title: Archiving Files and Searching and Extracting Data
steps.summary: Compress, archive and unzip data, then redirect and pipe command output and search files with grep and regular expressions.

steps.title: Turning Commands into Scripts and Choosing an Operating System
steps.summary: Turn command lines into executable shell scripts with arguments and exit codes, then weigh the operating system choices available to you.

steps.title: Understanding Computer Hardware and Where Data Is Stored
steps.summary: Power supplies, motherboards, memory, processors and storage devices, plus the Linux kernel, device files, processes and system logging.

steps.title: Your Computer on the Network and Basic Security
steps.summary: IPv4, IPv6, DNS and sockets on the wire, then the account types and privilege model that keep a Linux system safe.

steps.title: Creating Users and Groups, and Managing Permissions and Ownership
steps.summary: Create and manage accounts and groups with the passwd family of tools, and control access with symbolic and numeric file permission modes.

steps.title: Special Directories and Files
steps.summary: Temporary directories, hidden files, hard links and symbolic links: the special places a Linux filesystem uses to keep itself tidy.
